definitions.explanation: Describes doing or deciding something before the right time has come. Almost always appears in the set phrase {時期尚早|じきしょうそう}.

examples.japanese: それは{時期尚早|じきしょうそう}だ。
{結論|けつろん}を{出|だ}すのはまだ{時期尚早|じきしょうそう}だ。
examples.english: It's still too early to draw a conclusion.

examples.japanese: {市場|しじょう}の{状況|じょうきょう}を{考|かんが}えると、{投資|とうし}は{時期尚早|じきしょうそう}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: Given market conditions, I think investing would be premature.

notes:
Almost always used in the set phrase {時期尚早|じきしょうそう} ("the time is too early"), as a predicate (〜だ). {尚早|しょうそう} rarely stands alone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時期尚早|じきしょうそう}だ: it's premature; too early
- {時期尚早|じきしょうそう}との{声|こえ}: voices saying it's premature

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {早計|そうけい}: hasty (judgment) — emphasizes jumping to conclusions too quickly
- {早|はや}すぎる: too early — plain and everyday
